A local workspace for writers

Revise your manuscript.
Keep the research in reach.

See why a passage was flagged, compare a revision, and keep characters and sources beside your text. Lixity works on your computer with your Markdown or plain-text manuscript.

Watch the product tour ↓ Try a passage in browser →

Fictional English manuscript. Interactive read-only demo. No account or upload required.

From a marked passage to the next revision

Read, write, and check what changes in the text. Built-in analysis runs offline. Optional speech, map services, and connected AI clients have their own network and data-handling requirements.

Revise without losing your place

Keep your review marks by the text as you write with local autosave. Compare the draft with the saved manuscript under the same analysis settings before applying it.

Editor scope and availability (English)

See why the text was marked

Open a note about sentence rhythm, quotations, or repeated words and inspect the counted text. Compare chapters and follow available evidence back to the prose to decide what deserves a closer read.

How Lixity measures text

Follow a character through the manuscript

Draft a dossier from the prose and review its chapter distribution and passages in context. Keep your notes, claims, and exact source quotations beside the text.

Research, dossiers and evidence (English)

Share the version you checked

In the development build, download the selected dossier version as an A4 PDF with its saved notes, tables, excerpts, and source quotations. For the manuscript, choose a print layout or prepare a reading website with chapter limits and spoiler controls.

View a sample dossier PDF (English)Reading copy (English)
“

Inspect the signal. Make your own decision.

Measurements describe patterns in the supplied text. They do not grade literary quality or tell you how to rewrite a passage. Inspect the counted words and sentences, read them in context, and decide whether a difference matters.

How Lixity compares

Use Lixity to compare prose patterns, inspect the counted text, and trace research links while you read. It complements writing and planning tools; its measurements support your review and do not replace an editor.

FocusLixityDesktop suites (e.g. Papyrus Autor, Scrivener)OSS novel tools (e.g. novelWriter, Manuskript, bibisco)Cloud style tools (e.g. ProWritingAid, AutoCrit)Scene planners (e.g. Fictionary, Plottr)

Characters, scenes & dossiersCharacter and scene drafts extracted from prose; linked dossiers, collections, timelines, and mapsCharacter database, mind map & corkboard; maintained manuallyCharacter sheets, tags & corkboard; maintained manuallyNo character or scene dossiersTimelines, scene cards, and character arcs; planning only, without prose analysis
Sources & draft historyLocal archive for text, PDFs, images and video. Link sources to passages and compare drafts.Research folders & corkboards, without direct source links tied to draft historyProject notes, tags & plot trees, without a source archive or draft-level metricsNo built-in research archiveCharacter & plot notes without linked original sources
Privacy & offlineManuscripts and built-in analysis stay local and offline; optional online tools only on clickLocal storage & offline writing; occasional vendor license checks100% local & offline (plain text, Markdown, or local database), no cloud lock-inCloud processing with an account and internet connectionLocal or cloud storage depending on the app (e.g. Plottr desktop, Fictionary online)

Bring your own manuscript.

Install Lixity locally on Windows, macOS, or Linux. Open any Markdown or plain-text draft by following the setup guide.

Installation guide (English)
uv tool install --python 3.12 --managed-python lixity

This command installs the package published on PyPI. The demo and source documentation describe development version v0.9.0.

Latest published release · v0.9.0 release notes

Seven languages. One studio.

The site and app interface are available in seven languages. Choose the manuscript analysis language explicitly; technical documentation remains in English.

Website measurement (English)

This public website uses GoatCounter to count page visits and named demo, installation, repository and PDF links. The adapter sends public page paths and event names, excluding query strings, fragments, form contents and manuscript selections. The local app and exported manuscript reports contain no such measurement.

Language and appearance choices are stored locally in this browser when storage is available. Browser language is used only to suggest a public introduction; it is not sent to a translation service or used to change manuscript analysis.

Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control disable collection. Counts are approximate and do not establish installations or active authors. GoatCounter receives technical request data; see its privacy information. For questions, use the contact below.
